# INTENT

## User Request

Redesign the front page by removing the current hero and "Why use us" sections and replacing them with a vertical, branching explanation of the two menu products and their shared setup journey.

## Requested Outcome

The page starts with "Want your menu digital?", lets visitors compare Image Menu and Web Page Menu paths, merges the paths for shared benefits, and splits again to explain how each menu type is updated.

## Constraints

- Preserve Navigation, Who Are We, FAQ, and Footer.
- Prioritize mobile visitors arriving through QR-code scans.
- Include working example links for both menu choices.
- Keep English, Spanish, Italian, and Croatian localized.

## Open Questions

None. The user approved `/example` for the Web Page Menu and `https://hostingqr.com/paname` is the existing Image Menu example.

## Approved Refinement

Remove the HostingQr label, slightly reduce the opening question, and show lightweight static menu examples inside phone mockups within both product choices. The phones may still open the full examples when selected.

Add richer visuals to the shared Translations, QR Code, and Google Maps steps: a multilingual sample, a real QR code, and a compact business-map listing with a Menu action.

Move all three shared-step visuals to the left, remove their small icons, and replace the translation list with the existing menu artwork plus an animated top-right language flag.

Apply the supplied reference's editorial visual direction across the journey: serif headings, introductory subtitle, warm ivory background with soft sage shapes, flatter glass cards, curved connector joints, milestone nodes, arrow details, and wider desktop product-card compositions. Preserve the latest visual-left/no-icon shared-card direction.

Remove all remaining card icons and connector milestone icons, merge the two final editing branches into one shared Easy changes step, and end the journey with a localized WhatsApp/email contact callout.

Replace the animated menu-image translation preview with the supplied reference's static white list of four spread language options.

Compact the top of the journey so the free setup row fits into the initial desktop viewport, remove italics from the accented headline word, and highlight the localized free keyword in both setup titles.

Further refine the phone's top bezel and restyle the existing FAQ accordion to match the journey's editorial typography, soft glass surfaces, sage controls, and mobile-friendly spacing without changing FAQ content.

Remove the dining-experience marketing sentence, add immediate mobile-visible pricing navigation beneath the headline, and replace the Free redesign/setup flow arrows with a design icon and gear icon before their highlighted titles.
